(i) hot charge-carrier electoluminescence from the laser nanostructure is possible in both spontaneous and stimulated emission, and (ii) the intersubband absorption of IR radiation in the tunnel-coupled QW structure is possible under the heating of the carriers by the lateral electric field and high-power optical exciation.

the hot charge-carrier electrouminescence in quantum-well lasers is a result of the heating of charge carriers by the lateral field and the optical gain is the result of a combination of stimulated and spontaneous recombination of hot charge carriers.
the absorption and luminescence of hot charge carriers in quantum-well heterostructures are strongly dependent on the charge carrier concentration and the electric current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of the hot charge-carrier electrodynamics of semiconductor structures and the development of new types of semiconductor laser and photodetector devices
the study of the dynamics of nonequilibrium charge carriers in quantum-well structures and the influence of this dynamics on the optical properties of quantum-well lasers.
charge-carrier heating in laser heterostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charge carriers in the laser heterostructure are heated by the electric field and that this heating is enhanced by the presence of the optical field.
the charge-carrier heating and cooling processes have a significant impact on the performance of quantum-well lasers.
the results presented in the paper are in a good agreement with the theoretical predictions and experimental data obtained in the previous works.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hot-electron effect in quantum well laser heterostructures can be used to increase the laser output power by 1.5-2 times.
the hot-carrier electroluminance in the quantum-well heterostructure is the result of the interaction between hot electrons and LO phonons.

the charge-carrier heating in the quantum-well heterostructures is due to the electron-electron scattering and the electron-impurity scattering, and the carrier heating is more efficient in the stimulated emission mode than in the spontaneous emission mode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hot-electron absorption in quantum wells is an efficient method for the generation of high-energy charge carriers.
hot-carrier electroluminisence can be used for the study of carrier heating and carrier concentration in quantum wells.
